oil.summary: Crude pulled back sharply on Friday after a blistering weekly run, with WTI settling just below $100 (-2.55%) and Brent at $105.06 (-2.42%), yet both benchmarks remain up roughly 9-10% on the week and nearly 20% on the month. The selloff looks technical after WTI tagged an intraday high above $101 earlier in the session. The macro bid stays firmly intact: Houthi strikes are threatening Saudi Arabia's oil export bypass infrastructure, the U.S. military destroyed five Iranian tankers following attacks on a Navy warship, and Ukraine drone strikes are materially degrading Russian refining capacity per the IEA. RBC Capital's Helima Croft flagged a path to $120 Brent if the Middle East conflict persists. RBOB gasoline's outsized -7.31% drop stands out and may reflect end-of-driving-season demand seasonality.
drivers: Houthi strikes targeting Saudi oil export infrastructure and U.S.-Iran naval exchanges raising Hormuz/supply disruption risk
IEA confirms Ukraine drone strikes are degrading Russian refining capacity, tightening global refined product supply
Sharp RBOB gasoline selloff (-7.31%) diverges from crude, suggesting seasonal demand weakness at the pump even as flat-price crude risk premium holds

gas.summary: Natural gas price action today was divergent across regions. Henry Hub (NG) eased -0.88% to $2.809/MMBtu and is down 3.57% on the week, suggesting U.S. domestic fundamentals remain loose. European TTF, by contrast, dipped only -0.67% on the day but has surged 13.49% on the week and 33.56% over the past month to €81.5/MWh, reflecting tightened LNG availability amid the broader Middle East conflict backdrop. The sole U.S.-focused headline notes Jeff Currie calling for $5 gasoline before midterms and flagging diesel above $6/gallon nationally for the first time on record — a distillate squeeze with knock-on implications for gas-to-oil substitution. Headline flow for this sector is thin beyond that single data point.
drivers: Henry Hub remains pressured by domestic oversupply, falling 3.57% on the week despite geopolitical noise
European TTF has rallied 33.56% in a month, driven by Middle East supply risk squeezing global LNG flows
Jeff Currie's $5 gasoline / $6 diesel call signals broader energy cost pressure that could feed into industrial gas demand dynamics

power.summary: EU carbon (EUA) was effectively unchanged on the day (+0.11%) at €81.46/EUA, with a modest weekly gain of +2.85% and +4.16% on the month — a relatively subdued move given the turbulence in the underlying fuel complex. TTF's continued elevation at €81.5/MWh keeps gas-fired generation costs high, which should in principle support carbon prices as coal switches in at the margin. Two notable non-price developments: UK business groups formally called for removal of electricity bill taxes to restore competitiveness, and the UAE is reconsidering its planned 5-GW AI data center campus in Abu Dhabi after Iran targeted U.S. assets in the Gulf — a signal that Gulf power infrastructure investment is now directly exposed to escalation risk. Direct power-sector headline flow is otherwise thin today.
drivers: EUA carbon flat on the day; TTF at €81.5/MWh sustains high gas-fired generation costs and underpins carbon switch-in economics
UK business lobby pushes to eliminate electricity taxes, flagging industrial competitiveness concerns under elevated power prices
UAE pausing 5-GW AI campus plans signals Gulf escalation risk is beginning to disrupt large-scale power infrastructure investment decisions
